summary.intent: Fix the structural failure where release-please's post-merge workflow attempted to push a synced Cargo.lock directly to protected main branch (always rejected by GH006), and unblock PR #548 whose Lint was failing due to stale release-as pins.
summary.outcome: PR #550 created with a two-part fix: a new pre-merge workflow (cargo-lock-release-sync.yml) that syncs Cargo.lock onto the release-please PR branch before merge, and a reworked post-merge fallback that opens a chore PR instead of pushing to main. PR #548 was unblocked by removing 7 stale release-as pins from release-please-config.json and completing the Cargo.lock sync (core + fuse crates).

repo: classic branch protection with enforce_admins:true + 13 required checks blocks all direct pushes to main, including from GitHub App tokens — per-App bypass actors only exist on rulesets, not classic protection
release-please does NOT auto-remove release-as pins after a release ships; removal is always manual (precedent: PR #521 chore(ci): break sdk changelog self-compare loop)
check-stale-release-as.js flags staleness via strict equality: release-as === manifest version
pr-release-preview.js (Section 7.5, lines 644-652) preserves release-as entries inherited from origin/main, so stale pins on main propagate to every PR branch and never auto-clear
cipherbox-desktop Rust crate (src-tauri/Cargo.toml) versions independently from the apps/desktop node package — Cargo.lock must be checked against Cargo.toml, not the node manifest
No CI job uses --locked on workspace builds, so a stale Cargo.lock does not break CI directly
The root workspace has a single Cargo.lock covering all 6 crates including cipherbox-desktop

code.finding: Bot preserves release-as entries from origin/main when building preview, causing stale pins to propagate indefinitely to all PR branches
Staleness check uses strict equality (release-as === manifest version), comparing release-please-config.json against .release-please-manifest.json

workflow: git verify-commit showing 'N' status does not mean unsigned — it means allowedSignersFile is not configured locally; SSH signatures are still present
When diagnosing CI failures, read the actual log output rather than assuming the reported symptom matches the hypothesis — the #548 Lint failure was release-as pins, not Cargo.lock
Pre-merge workflow hooks on pull_request with synchronize trigger are idempotent-safe for release-please PR branches since release-please force-pushes re-trigger them
zizmor requires permission-contents: write scoped to jobs that push, and flags github-app token scope as High severity

friction: Multiple bash commands were needed to get a simple Cargo.lock vs Cargo.toml comparison due to shell variable scoping issues across tool calls
Initial diagnosis incorrectly flagged cipherbox-desktop Cargo.lock as stale by comparing against the node manifest version (0.44.0) instead of the Rust crate version (0.35.0)

The post-merge retry/rebase loop in release-please.yml was silently futile — logs showed 'Current branch main is up to date' before each GH006 rejection, masking that the failure was structural not transient
actionlint had a pre-existing SC2129 style nit on an untouched step that couldn't be cleanly fixed in scope
open_items: The node-manifest-vs-Rust-crate version gap for cipherbox-desktop (apps/desktop 0.44.0 vs crates/cipherbox-desktop 0.35.0) may indicate a release-please extra-files propagation issue — flagged but not investigated
PR #550 (cargo-lock-release-sync fix) was created but not yet merged — needs review and merge before next Rust crate release
PR #548 (staging-kubo-tuning) had commit staged but not yet pushed at end of transcript — needs push to complete unblocking
Migrating from classic branch protection to rulesets would enable per-App bypass actors and simplify future release automation, but was explicitly deferred as posture-weakening
